text: A packet operator is a linear map written between the members of a finite direct sum. We study the resulting computational representation before choosing a processor or kernel. Exact formulas are given for block sparse application, block diagonal plus low rank algebra, Woodbury inversion, support propagation, block preconditioning, and packetwise perturbation. Products of low rank corrections admit optimal recompression through a small singular value problem, with explicit error propagation through a product chain. A rooted candidate decomposition supports an exact compiler when representation cost and error are additive. Dynamic programming gives the optimal Lagrangian pruning, an exact quantized error budget algorithm, and a local update rule. Discrete precision assignment becomes a multiple choice budget problem. Arithmetic, storage, data movement, launch count, discovery, transfer, and materialization are kept as separate costs. A preserved corpus of 154 recorded CPU and GPU measurements illustrates regular packet gains, precision frontiers, crossover behavior, and retained negative controls. Its largest reported structured ratio is 14.89 against a device resident dense GPU calculation, with archived matching-metadata limitations stated explicitly.
